core.prompt: A student says: “n² is even, so n is even, because squaring an even number gives an even number.” Is the claim true, and is that argument enough? Repair it.
Over the integers, compare: (A) for every x there exists y with y>x; (B) there exists y such that for every x, y>x. Which are true?
Explain why a decimal integer is divisible by 11 iff its alternating digit sum is divisible by 11.
For integers n, assess both claims: if 4 divides n then 2 divides n; if 2 divides n then 4 divides n.
Negate precisely: “For every integer n there exists an integer m with m>n.” Is the original statement true?
For which digit d is the decimal number 4d2 divisible by 9?
Negate: “For every real x, P(x) holds.” Negate: “There exists a real x for which P(x) holds.”
State the tests for divisibility by 3 and 9 for a nonnegative integer in decimal notation.

branches.prompt: For integers n, is “3 divides n implies 6 divides n” true? Justify.
Integers a,b satisfy: ab is divisible by 6. Must at least one of a,b be divisible by 6? Give a counterexample or proof, and explain which prime-divisibility fact still holds.
Negate “Every student solved at least one question.” Keep the student/question domains unchanged.
For real a, when is this true: for every real x there exists real y such that y²=x+a? Negate the statement and decide it for every a.
Is the decimal number 513 divisible by 9? Explain without long division.
A number written in base 8 has digits d_m…d_0. Derive a digit test for divisibility by 7 and one for divisibility by 9.
